serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText:
Free Bo Brogan podcast? He’s super popular these days, but I never really listened to him before.
My antivirus says this link is safe so I guess I will give it a short listen.
Aaaand…
It’s on.
Bo: Yo! Welcome back to my podcast, very excited today…
Bo: Jamie, check for me really quick if there are any new monkey versus human fights on live leak.
Jamie: No Bo… There is none.
Bo: That’s crazy man! Humans are just scared! It’s entirely possible that people are just instinctively avoiding bigger and stronger primates.
Jamie: …
Bo: ...Getting back to the business. Profesor Nigevchenko! Yo man! What’s up?
Nigevchenko: *Heavy breathing* I’m ok Bo.
Bo: You look terrible man! What’s that on your face?
Nigevchenko: That’s an oxygen mask Bo… I have terminal lung cancer and I need this mask to help me breathe.
Bo: Woah! Jamie, pull that up. Google: ‘death rate of terminal cancer’.
Jamie: It’s saying here it’s 100%.
Bo: No way! Source?
Jamie: MedicalExaminer.ic
Bo: Well…{{wi}} They are kinda biased these days. 
Bo: But it makes sense. Like, it’s terminal, right? It’s terminal cancer. So, like, you can’t really cure it. So it totally makes sense that you are supposed to die from it.
Bo: So… Professor Nigelchenko, Nigenchenko? Agh, I have a problem with russian names.
Nigevchenko: It’s Nigevchenko…{{wi}} And I’m Ukrainian.
Bo: Yeah, right. {{wi}}Wanna smoke something? Last time Tom Crews smoked so much we had to call for his cult to pick him up! Great time…
Nigevchenko: I cannot smoke.
Bo: What a party pooper man. You vegan?
Nigevchenko: No.
Bo: Oh man, you missed out. It’s a great diet I’m telling you. You need to supplement some vitamins, but after some time and terrible bowel pain it’s actually the best thing you can do for your health.
Nigevchenko: Well *coughs* I think it’s too late for that in my case.
Bo: Oh, right. {{wi}}Then I guess I will not bother you with gluten…
Nigevchenko: …
Bo: *cracks up with laughter* 
Bo: Oh man, we have a great time together. Wanna drink some whiskey? I got some great hundred year old whiskey from Mississippi.
Nigevchenko: I’m ill Bo, that’s not a good idea.
Bo: *takes a sip*
Bo: So… You are a physicist. 
Nigevchenko: *coughs* Astrophysicist, theoretical physicist. I have spent good portion of my life *inhales* constructing a model of this universe…
Bo: Yeah, I wanted to talk about it, your theory. ‘Layer theory’ or something like that.
Nigevchenko: ‘Theory of layering fabric of reality’
Bo: Yeah, yeah, tell us about it!
Nigevchenko: It’s a theory that I began developing in London in 1975 after I recovered from losing both my big toes in Soviet gulag. 
Nigevchenko: The whole principle of this theorem is based…
Bo: *Bo cracks up again* No, please, continue. 
Nigevchenko: The main idea is that reality is layered up *coughs*. Is layered up on the basis of the speed of expansion of the universe. It’s creating something like a gradient, but its surfaces are distorted by ever changing gravitational pulls of heavy matter.
Bo: Woah! That would be, like, blackholes, right?
Nigevchenko: Among others, yeah *coughs horribly* 
Bo: Did smoke from my bong got to you? Sorry man. 
Bo: Jamie, do you remember this elephant that painted the Milky Way? Pull that shit up. We will watch it until professor Nagevchenko will get his composure back.
Nigevchenko: *still is horribly coughing*
Bo: See that elephant? Woah.
Bo: Just how detailed was that painting?
Jamie: Geographic Journal said it’s super detailed. A lot of details yeah.
Bo: Imagine all this money we spend on space exploration, observation of the stars and here a fucking elephant just paints whole star map with a trunk. Crazy man.
Nigevchenko: *chokes*
Bo: Is this the same elephant that suffocated himself by farting in his own trunk?
Jamie: Give me a moment.
Jamie: ...
Jamie: That was a different elephant, an Indian one. Painter was African.
Bo: Oh, yeah, that makes sense. There is that thing, right. Genetic memory. It’s entirely possible that african elephants know stars and shit better, because in Africa there are less trees, right? It’s savannah, S A V A N N A H. Pronunciation is really hard.
Bo: Without trees elephants just look at the stars at night and through thousands of years they just learned this shit. It’s entirely possible.
Nigevchenko: *falls to the ground*
Bo: WOAH! You alright there Negerchenko?! Oh man, he fell like Renan Barao after a spinning thrust kick from Wineland!
Bo: Jamie, fast! Pull up how to aid a dying man… {{wi}}Is that adrenaline shot gluten free?
Announcer: That’s the end of the episode 3262 of Bo Brogan Podcast. Thank you for listening. After the first listening link in mail will expire.
You: …
You: I can’t believe millions of people are listening to this dude…
